_source: Captured verbatim from a live claim-review of atmin-inc/review PR #2 on 2026-09-20, deepseek/deepseek-v3.2 over OpenRouter, head f8cce6c against base 91f4f45. Both claims are correct about the code. Both were refuted by rung 1 before b0425d9, because each carries a proposition about the account object's shape checked with body_contains inside renameAccount, where the deleted guard was the only mention of ownerId. Do not hand-edit to make a test pass: the point of the fixture is that a real emitter produced exactly this.

claims.description: The renameAccount function updates account.displayName without checking if actorId matches account.ownerId
claims.suspectedCondition: When renameAccount is called with an actorId that does not match the account's ownerId

evidenceToCheck.proposition: The function signature includes actorId parameter
The account object has ownerId property
Before the change, there was an owner check that threw 'Forbidden'
After the change, the owner check is missing

claims.description: Any user can modify any account's displayName without ownership verification, allowing unauthorized data modification
claims.suspectedCondition: When a non-owner calls renameAccount with a valid accountId

evidenceToCheck.proposition: Function modifies account.displayName without checking actorId matches account.ownerId
Function signature includes actorId parameter suggesting caller authentication intent
No authorization check exists in the function
